introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II, answer all questions choosing EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown: State the laws of reflection. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
1. The **incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal** to the mirror at the point of incidence all lie **in the same plane**.

2. The **angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection** ($i = r$), both measured from the normal.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Draw a ray diagram to show how the eye sees the image of an object in a plane mirror. *[3 marks]*

(ii) State two characteristics of this image. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Diagram (to be drawn by the candidate):** draw the mirror as a vertical line (hatched on the back) and a point object O in front of it. Draw **two rays** from O that hit the mirror at different points; at each point draw the normal (dotted) and the **reflected ray with angle of reflection equal to the angle of incidence**. Place the **eye** where the two reflected rays enter it. Produce the reflected rays **backwards behind the mirror with dotted lines**: they meet at the image I, as far behind the mirror as O is in front of it, with the line OI perpendicular to the mirror. Mark arrowheads on the real rays only (from O to the mirror, then to the eye).

(ii) Any two: the image is **virtual** (cannot be formed on a screen); **upright**; **same size** as the object; **laterally inverted**; **as far behind the mirror as the object is in front**.
